terms.gloss: monthly, happening every month; lasting a month
terms.comment: The adjective: monthly interest, a monthly holiday, the moon’s monthly course. As a noun, mēnstrua n. pl. are the menses (see period).

evidence: Col. 11.1.21: bis singulīs mēnsibus, twice a month (Lewis & Short, s.v. recēnseō)
terms.comment: The adverb “monthly”: singulīs mēnsibus, each month; in singulōs mēnsēs, for each month, per month, as in singulōs diēs (Dig. 36.2.12, Lewis & Short).
Formed like quotannīs, every year; the lawyers’ phrase.

phrases.latin: tū cursū, dea, mēnstruō mētiēns iter annuum
phrases.english: you, goddess, measuring out the year’s journey with your monthly course
We go to Grandpa’s every month.

sources: Lewis & Short: menstruus · Lewis & Short: mensis · Lewis & Short: quot
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. monthly.
